new_entities.description: Use of letrozole as a first-line ovulation-induction treatment in women with anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome.

new_entities.name: Live birth rate
new_entities.description: The probability of delivering a live infant after fertility treatment or conception.

edges.effect_quant: The clearest pooled estimate now comes from the 2023 Obstetrics & Gynecology meta-analysis, where letrozole improved live birth versus clomiphene citrate (RR 1.49, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.74). This closely matches the earlier Cochrane estimate (OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.42 to 1.99) and large trial data.
edges.population: women with infertility due to anovulatory polycystic ovary syndrome undergoing first-line ovulation induction
edges.mechanism: Letrozole lowers estrogen feedback and increases endogenous FSH drive without the same anti-estrogenic endometrial effects often associated with clomiphene. That tends to support more favorable follicular development and implantation conditions, which helps explain why live birth benefits are stronger than a simple ovulation-count story.
edges.summary: This is one of the stronger reproductive edges in the corpus. Letrozole has moved beyond being a plausible alternative and now has repeated comparative evidence showing higher live-birth success than clomiphene in anovulatory PCOS.
edges.caveats: Most evidence is comparative against clomiphene rather than placebo, so the claim is about first-line treatment superiority rather than spontaneous fertility restoration. Live-birth gains can still vary by BMI, phenotype, and whether intercourse or IUI follows induction.
